title: Contrastive learning
reading: The slide states the core objective of contrastive learning: maximize similarities of positive pairs and minimize similarities of negative pairs. Below, a schematic shows a two-encoder (key/query) setup feeding a similarity matrix used as the loss, with two annotated update strategies — weight sharing versus momentum (moving-average) updating of the key encoder, the latter given by an equation.

visuals.description: A key image and a query image each pass through a green trapezoidal Encoder; their outputs meet at a 5x5 similarity grid with the diagonal cells shaded blue, labelled 'loss'. A red arrow flows back from the loss to the query encoder ('Update encoder q'). Left annotation: 'Share weights for both encoder'; right annotation: 'Update encoder k by moving average' with the equation θ_k ≔ m θ_k + (1 − m) θ_q.
visuals.assertion: Contrastive training compares encoded key and query batches in a similarity matrix whose diagonal entries are the positives; the query encoder is trained by gradients while the key encoder is either weight-shared or updated as a momentum moving average of the query encoder's parameters.

concepts.name: Positive and negative pairs
concepts.why_it_matters: Defines what the contrastive objective pulls together and pushes apart.

concepts.name: Momentum encoder update
concepts.why_it_matters: Gives a slowly-evolving, consistent key encoder without backpropagating through it.

concepts.name: Similarity matrix / contrastive loss
concepts.why_it_matters: Implements the objective over a batch, with diagonal as positives.
